question.text: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of solute A was dissolved in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>62</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> of ethanol and freezing point of the solution was found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>155</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. The molar mass of solute <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>gmol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. [Given: Freezing point of ethanol is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>156</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>. Density of ethanol is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>cm</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Freezing point depression constant of ethanol is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>00</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>]

solution.text:
Given

Mass of C2H5OH=62.5×0.8=50 g 

Mass of solute = 1.80 g

Depression in freezing point ∆Tf = 156.0-155.1 = 0.9 K

We know that the depression in freezing point

ΔTf=Kf×m

0.9=2×1.8×1000Mw×50

Mw=2×1.8×10000.9×50=80
